library_support.name: General GNU APL/PCRE2 literal global substitution binding
library_support.reason: Accepts arbitrary pattern/replacement/subject strings. The adapter invokes standard pcre2_substitute, handles output buffer capacity and converts Unicode strings. It has no benchmark patterns, no count loop, no benchmark sequence, no length-only shortcut, and no I/O.
library_support.memory_strategy: The large subject is the direct APL right argument. C++ stores Unicode subject/output buffers; it does not allocate whole-length APL integer masks, prefix arrays, destination arrays or a per-match container. Only complete replacement text is returned. Arbitrary expanding replacements retry after PCRE2 reports required capacity.

programs.source_provenance: New memory-efficient counted APL application, retaining the original canonical orchestration and nine GNU APL regex counts. General PCRE2 substitution binding is provided through the published GNU APL native-library interface.

adaptations: Explicit GNU APL implementation with every application helper counted.
General output launcher preserves application fd 3 without byte transformation; interpreter diagnostics and its automatic exit newline go to stderr.
Avoid packing/disclosing the large subject: the general substitute interface receives it directly as the right argument.
Clear original Input after header/newline removal; retain only its scalar length.
Use actual general PCRE2 global literal substitution in place of per-match concatenation or full-length APL masks/prefix/scatter arrays.

The advance variant uses the same impossible-candidate guard as the pinned Rust #4 source; no alternative pi algorithm or digit cache.

Four source functions: coefficient, apply, apply-transpose, and step. Twenty power-method applications execute forty matrix-vector products. Coefficients are computed by emitted Mech arithmetic; no stored matrix or answer shortcut.

The Mech-defined callback performs double-precision escape iteration for every pixel, with a maximum of 50 iterations, and emits the complete PBM. Native SIMD and lane termination preserve that algorithm.

Nine independent regex counts, each using its prescribed pattern, and five ordered regex substitutions. The general regex library handles each operation; there is no combined-pattern benchmark matcher.

Full bottom-up construction and traversal of distinct ordinary nodes, including equally allocated leaves. Uses the general core library memory pool through memory/with-arena and memory/with-frame. This allocation strategy must be disclosed; it is not a default-GC comparison.
